title: Countable products in derived categories
statement: Let A be an abelian category with exact countable products and derived category D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Countable products [def-weil-category-product] exist in D(A), the image under Q of every termwise product cone is limiting, and each homology functor preserves countable discrete limits.

proof.text: For (2), choose complexes $C_i$ representing $K_i$ and let $\prod_iC_i$ be the termwise product with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i$. Exactness of countable products makes the products of the short exact sequences $0\to Z^p\to C^p\to B^{p+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^p\to Z^p\to H^p\to0$ exact, so $Z^p$, $B^p$ and $H^p$ commute with products: $H^p(\prod_iC_i)=\prod_iH^p(C_i)$, and a product of quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism. A chain map into a termwise product, and a chain homotopy, are exactly families of component chain maps and homotopies, so $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(L,\prod_iN_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(L,N_i)$. Quasi-isomorphisms form a multiplicative system in $K(\mathcal A)$ with localization $D(\mathcal A)$ [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so every morphism $Q(X)\to Q(Y)$ is $Q(s)^{-1}Q(f)$ for a quasi-isomorphism $s:Y\to M$ and $f:X\to M$, and $Q(s)^{-1}Q(f)=0$ if and only if $uf\simeq0$ for some quasi-isomorphism $u:M\to M'$ [lem-pc-left-localization-hom-colimit]. Existence (the argument of Tag 07KC): given $\alpha_i=Q(s_i)^{-1}Q(f_i):L\to C_i$ with $s_i:C_i\to M_i$, the product $s=\prod_is_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\alpha=Q(s)^{-1}Q(\prod_if_i)$ satisfies $Q(\mathrm{pr}_i)\alpha=\alpha_i$, because $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ s=s_i\circ\mathrm{pr}_i$. Uniqueness: let $\alpha=Q(s)^{-1}Q(f):L\to\prod_iC_i$, $s:\prod_iC_i\to M$, with $Q(\mathrm{pr}_i)\alpha=0$ for all $i$. Write $Q(\mathrm{pr}_i)Q(s)^{-1}=Q(t_i)^{-1}Q(g_i)$ with $t_i:C_i\to N_i$ a quasi-isomorphism and $g_i:M\to N_i$; then $Q(g_is)=Q(t_i\mathrm{pr}_i)$ and $Q(g_if)=0$, so after composing $t_i,g_i$ with a later quasi-isomorphism out of $N_i$ we have $g_is\simeq t_i\mathrm{pr}_i$ and $g_if\simeq0$. With $g=(g_i)_i:M\to\prod_iN_i$ and the quasi-isomorphism $t=\prod_it_i$, componentwise homotopies give $gs\simeq t$ and $gf\simeq0$, so $Q(s)^{-1}=Q(t)^{-1}Q(g)$ and $\alpha=Q(t)^{-1}Q(gf)=0$. As $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}$ is additive, $\prod_iC_i$ with the $Q(\mathrm{pr}_i)$ is the product of the $K_i$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-category-product], for any choice of representatives.

theorem derivedCategory_countableProducts_core
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [CountableAB4Star A] :
    ∃ hP : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A),
      letI : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory A) := hP
      (∀ (J : Type t) [Countable J] (C : J → CochainComplex A ℤ),
        Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone (limit.cone (Discrete.functor C))))) ∧
      (∀ (J : Type t) [Countable J] (p : ℤ),
        PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A p))
